source.title: Architext: Language-Driven Generative Architecture Design
source.authors: Theodoros Galanos; Antonios Liapis; Georgios N. Yannakakis

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: It compares downstream layout-generation metrics across differently sized models, using measures unlike held-out pretraining loss. It does not measure a power-law loss curve.
record.gate_note: The study reports validity and correctness by model and prompt category; these are recorded as separate rows. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy, fit scaling laws, test extrapolation, or assess a compute-optimal allocation. Diversity results are not included as rows because diversity is not a measure named by the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes four pretrained LMs (125M to 6B) on a synthetic floor-plan task and compares downstream correctness and validity by model size. Assessing the effect of scale is a stated aim (Methodology goal 3). That makes it a new-setting result bearing on V6. It fits no scaling curve and measures no loss, and size is confounded with architecture and pretraining corpus (GPT-J was trained on the Pile), so it is T3 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The conclusion states that scaling model size boosts semantic accuracy 'without affecting design diversity'. It calls a full scaling-laws study of model and data size open future work. Validity is above 99.5% for all models and reaches 100% for GPT-J.
record.recipe_differences: This is a fine-tuned architectural layout-generation evaluation across model sizes, not a held-out language-model loss sweep or compute-allocation study.
record.method_sensitivity: Correctness varies substantially by prompt category; the authors note especially low performance on out-of-distribution room-count/location requests. Model size, architecture, pretraining, and fine-tuning setup vary together.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-J has a much higher out-of-distribution layout ratio in AP, AN and LU, and greater OOD spatial diversity (Tables 3 and 4). Its OOD ratio collapses in RG and LNU (0.68%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Output diversity of fine-tuned generative LMs changes non-uniformly with model scale.

record.problems: Only four models are compared, and size is confounded with architecture, pretraining corpus, and training setup. No held-out pretraining loss, uncertainty estimates, or controlled scaling sweep are reported. The task uses a synthetic residential-layout dataset and a limited set of prompt types.
record.rows_left_out: No table results were omitted. Diversity measurements in Tables 3 and 4 were not included because they measure output diversity rather than the loss or downstream task performance specified by the claim versions.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss and no power-law fit.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Fine-tuning is used but no power-law loss or performance curve is measured.
Prediction from pretraining loss; functional form or smoothness of the improvement (only 3 distinct sizes, confounded); any prediction of the 6B result from the smaller models.
No fitted exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The record's labels lumped the AN reversal with the validity ceiling under one limits_scope; these are now split. The record also did not note that the clean same-family comparison (GPT2-S to GPT2-M) shows no gain. The paper's own summary misattributes 83% to RS (it is RG; RS is 51.81, about 7x). The intro says GPT-J ranges 30 to 83% while Table 2 gives 25 to 84%. The authors acknowledge that the Pile pretraining and architecture confound the size effect. There are no uncertainty estimates, and sample sizes per category are 600 to 1600. The rows are per-model values, so states were set relative to the smaller-model baselines.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or compute, including power-law form and orders of magnitude.
Prediction of larger-run loss from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Controlled comparisons of depth, width, and other architectural details at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss behavior across other modalities or training regimes; fine-tuning is used, but no loss law is measured.
The study evaluates layout-generation correctness and validity across model sizes, but does not test predictability from pretraining loss or establish a general scaling curve.
Dependence of fitted exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup or fitting choices, and bending of loss curves.

relationships.condition: GPT-J-6B versus the 125M to 355M models, correctness in RG, RS, AP, LU and LNU
relationships.reason: Large gains (e.g. RG 83.73 vs about 15; LU 25.00 vs about 1). But size is confounded with architecture and the Pile pretraining corpus. Rows V6-CORR-GPTJ-RG/RS/AP/LU/LNU.
relationships.display_finding: GPT-J-6B achieved RG correctness of 83.73 versus about 15 and LU correctness of 25.00 versus about 1, with architecture and pretraining corpus confounded with size.

relationships.condition: Same-family GPT2-Small (125M) to GPT2-Medium (355M); validity metric
relationships.reason: A 2.8x size increase gives no correctness gain in any category, so improvement appears only at the confounded 6B jump. Validity sits at ceiling and moves by under 0.5 points. Rows V6-CORR-GPT2M-*, V6-VALID-GPT2M-*, V6-VALID-GPTJ-*.
relationships.display_finding: A 2.8-fold size increase produced no correctness gains, validity changed by under 0.5 points near ceiling, and correctness improved only at the confounded 6B jump.

relationships.condition: Negative-adjacency (AN) prompts, GPT-J-6B versus smaller models
relationships.reason: Correctness falls with scale, 56.61 vs about 60.6; row V6-CORR-GPTJ-AN.
relationships.display_finding: Correctness fell to 56.61 for GPT-J-6B from about 60.6 for smaller models.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Correctness on RG, RS, AP, LU, and LNU prompt categories; comparison of the 6-billion-parameter GPT-J with the smaller models
reader_labels.reason: GPT-J has substantially higher correctness in these categories than the smaller models; rows V6-CORR-GPTJ-RG, V6-CORR-GPTJ-RS, V6-CORR-GPTJ-AP, V6-CORR-GPTJ-LU, and V6-CORR-GPTJ-LNU.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Negative-adjacency correctness and validity across all prompt categories
reader_labels.reason: GPT-J's negative-adjacency correctness is lower than that of the smaller models, while validity is already at least 99.5% for all models and changes little with size; rows V6-CORR-GPTJ-AN and V6-VALID-NEO-RG through V6-VALID-GPTJ-LNU.
